hints: Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium: $T\sin\theta + 120\sin 45^\circ = 15g = 150\text{ N}$.
Divide the vertical equation by the horizontal equation to find $\tan\theta$ and calculate $\theta$, then use Pythagoras to find $T$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$T\cos\theta = 120\cos 45^\circ = 120\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right) = 60\sqrt{2} \approx 84.8528\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$T\sin\theta + 120\sin 45^\circ = 15g = 150 \implies T\sin\theta = 150 - 60\sqrt{2} \approx 65.1472\text{ N}$$

Divide the vertical component by the horizontal component to determine angle $\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{65.1472}{84.8528} \approx 0.767767 \implies \theta = \arctan(0.767767) \approx 37.5^\circ$$

Calculate the tension magnitude using Pythagoras' theorem:
$$T = \sqrt{(84.8528)^2 + (65.1472)^2} = \sqrt{7200 + 4244.16} = \sqrt{11444.16} \approx 107\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The block of mass $15\text{ kg}$ is in equilibrium suspended by two strings, under its weight $W = mg = 15 \times 10 = 150\text{ N}$ and tensions $120\text{ N}$ and $T$.

Sum forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$T\cos\theta = 120\cos 45^\circ$$
$$T\cos\theta = 120 \times 0.707107 = 84.8528\text{ N} \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Sum forces vertically in equilibrium:
$$T\sin\theta + 120\sin 45^\circ = 150$$
$$T\sin\theta = 150 - 120\sin 45^\circ = 150 - 84.8528 = 65.1472\text{ N} \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Divide Equation 2 by Equation 1 to eliminate $T$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{T\sin\theta}{T\cos\theta} = \frac{65.1472}{84.8528} \approx 0.767767$$
$$\theta = \arctan(0.767767) \approx 37.516^\circ \approx 37.5^\circ$$

Square and add Equation 1 and Equation 2 to find tension $T$:
$$T^2 = (T\cos\theta)^2 + (T\sin\theta)^2 = (84.8528)^2 + (65.1472)^2$$
$$T^2 = 7200 + 4244.16 = 11444.16$$
$$T = \sqrt{11444.16} \approx 106.977\text{ N} \approx 107\text{ N}$$
